messages:
maya: quick sync — we need to lock the console observability scope for next sprint. customers want dashboards, better cost breakdown, tracing hooks, and error analytics. capacity limited. proposals?

alex: my vote: ship small dashboard templates + per-route cost breakdown in M1. tracing hooks + span tagging in M2, full error analytics (root-cause UI) M3. keeps M1 thin and customer-visible. :thumbsup:

ryan: +1 for prioritizing cost visibility — we keep getting asks from Platform teams for per-model & per-route cost lines. can we surface token-level delta and cache savings?

maya: yes — key asks to satisfy for M1: (1) dashboard templates for common slices, (2) aggregated per-route cost panel (daily/7d), (3) simple error rate widget with top-5 error messages. not full investigations.

sasha: engineering constraints: tracing hooks require a small SDK change to emit service/span tags and sampling headers. estimating 3 dev-weeks + test harness. dashboards + cost panels are mostly frontend + queries work, ~2 dev-weeks.

diana: customer-driven must-haves: enterprise trial customer (AcmeHealth) needs cost breakdown and error alerts before we ship. they said trace-level context is negotiable for GA but mandatory for pilot.

alex: proposal for launch criteria (MVP):
- dashboard templates deployed in console
- cost breakdown query + export CSV
- error widget with alerting rule + sample rate >= 1% false-positive cap
- smoke test: load dashboard queries under 95th percentile latency target

maya: rollout plan: canary 5% for orgs with <10 users, monitor latency/cost telemetry for 48h, if no regression -> 25% -> GA. fallback flag to disable heavy cost queries.

observability-bot: deploybot: canary started for console-observability v0.1.0 -> groups: small-orgs. link: https://deploys/redwood/console-observability/0.1.0

ryan: regarding cost queries: add a cache layer or pre-aggregations to avoid high scan costs. we should add an internal limit and surface an explain plan to customers if query is expensive.

sasha: agree. we can implement a rollup table per-day/per-route and backfill for 30 days. low-risk.

diana: acceptance criteria for customers: AcmeHealth gets pilot access + weekly sync, we validate cost numbers vs their billing within 10%.

maya: risks: if tracing hooks slip, we need to document that incident investigation requires logs + sampling workaround. capture that in release notes.

alex: action items: @sasha start SDK trace header PR, @ryan design rollup schema and cost export, @diana coordinate AcmeHealth pilot and legal. I'll own dashboard templates + acceptance tests.

maya: good. I'll convert this to a short PRD and k-card by EOD. if anyone sees major pushback, call it out now.

observability-bot: reminder: next product/eng sync about this on 2025-06-23 10:00 UTC
